backlog.title: Macro endpoints graceful fail-close — return 200 + is_estimate=true + per-bloc blocked_reason on upstream-fetch failure instead of opaque HTTP 500
backlog.desc: VN-MACRO-TOOLING /goal#1 BEST-RESULT resilience gap (router F2). The 4 Zone-A macro endpoints (POST /trade-balance, /bop, /macro-indicators, /cpi-components) return HTTP 500 with an opaque error whenever the upstream NSO/SBV fetch (VPS-proxied, currently dark per F1) fails, instead of degrading honestly the way /liquidity-state is DOCUMENTED to. This is a resilience defect that persists even after the proxy is restored: any transient upstream failure must degrade gracefully, never opaque-500. GENERIC across all endpoints (/goal#2 — ONE fix pattern, mirror the intended liquidity fail-close).
backlog.root_cause: PO RAW-verified at code level: handlers_vmt_{trade,bop,macro,cpi}.go each do `resp, err := uc.Execute(...); if err != nil { w.WriteHeader(http.StatusInternalServerError); encode(resp); return }`. The use-case error builders errorTradeResponse / errorBOPResponse / errorMacroResponse / errorCPIResponse (pkg/application/usecases_vmt_{trade,bop,macro,cpi}.go) ALL return their populated degraded DTO TOGETHER WITH a non-nil `fmt.Errorf(...)`. Because Execute returns a non-nil error, the thin handler discards the carefully-populated fail-closed DTO and emits an opaque 500. errorLiquidityResponse has the SAME non-nil-error shape (same latent bug) — /liquidity-state only looks graceful in the live incident because its providers read local market.db (not geo-blocked) and hit the happy path; its error path would also 500.
backlog.fix_spec: Mirror the INTENDED liquidity fail-close pattern across ALL 5 macro use-cases. On UPSTREAM-FETCH failure (vpsFetch / NSO-Excel / SBV-HTML provider error or parse failure) — as distinct from a true programming/wiring fault (nil provider) — Execute MUST return (populatedDegradedResponse, nil): Status set to a non-error degraded value (e.g. "degraded" / "estimate"), every bloc IsEstimate=true, and each affected bloc's BlockedReason naming the unreachable source per bloc (e.g. "NSO customs Excel unreachable via VPS proxy 125.212.251.27:3128"). The thin HTTP handlers then emit HTTP 200 with the honest degraded payload. done.note: CONFIRMED (was 'suspected' 08:15Z, CONFIRMED 08:46Z same window). Mechanism: leader-lock owner_session token = pid-<pid>-ts-<startupTs>, regenerated per process. Cowork FIRE ticks run as separate gateway-proxied calls -> each tick sees a different owner_session -> when it re-reads an ALIVE lock it claimed on a PRIOR tick, the own-held heartbeat branch (which matches on owner_session equality) never matches -> falls through to the peer-held branch -> silent suppression of a legitimate FIRE. Evidence: 08:15Z chef-intraday MATCHED but re-claim returned claimed=false (lock alive from 08:00:44Z, ttl 1800s) -> PEER-HELD -> silent exit, YET slot token cowork-slot:chef-intraday claimed=true (no real peer) = contradiction. 08:45Z chef-eod fired clean precisely BECAUSE the 08:00Z lock had expired >1800s (stolen:true) = clean fresh claim. So: alive-lock => false peer-held suppression; expired-lock => correct fire. Benign 2026-06-05 (08:15Z intraday already fired 07:16Z) but LATENT product risk: any FIRE landing within 1800s of a prior leader claim by the same logical leader is dropped. FIX DIRECTION: make leader identity STABLE across per-tick gateway calls (durable leader id persisted in the lock store / coordination.db, not a per-process pid+startupTs), OR have the heartbeat/re-claim path treat 'lock held by my own logical leader key' as own-held regardless of session token. ROUTE: PO to confirm owner — leader-lock lives in the cowork dispatcher + mcp-server task-lock tool (coordination.db); likely dev-mcp-server (task_claim/leader-lock) + cowork-flow skill. Kin FU-LOCKSTORE-EXPIRED-GC, FU-CHEF-MARKER-INFLOW. Detected by dev-team tick 2026-06-05T09:10Z from drained cowork heartbeats. | DONE+LIVE 2026-06-05T10:xxZ. Root cause PROVEN by architect spike (VERDICT A, brief docs/architecture-briefs/2026-06-05-leader-lock-false-peer-held-spike.md): NOT 'owner_session regenerated per gateway call' (that theory was false — SERVER_SESSION_ID is process-stable) but owner_session NOT DURABLE ACROSS PROCESS RESTART. mcp-server restarted 08:11:38Z (FDA-1 deploy) 654s after cowork-leader claimed 08:00:44Z (owner_session pid-1-ts-1780613414482); new process minted a new SERVER_SESSION_ID -> 08:15Z heartbeat UPDATE WHERE owner_session=<new> matched 0 rows -> ok=false -> false PEER-HELD silent suppression. So EVERY deploy/restart silently orphaned the cowork-leader lock for up to its 1800s TTL. FIX (both layers, live): (1) mcp-server 1b058f40 — releaseOrphanTask + new MCP tool task_force_release_orphan(task_id,owner_agent,orphan_threshold_seconds=600,min120): force-releases a held lock ONLY when heartbeat_age>threshold (stale/dead holder); a FRESH heartbeat (live peer) is NOT released -> preserves the 2026-06-02 dup-spawn discriminator (no double-leader window). 8 new tests RED->GREEN (AC-SL-6/7), tsc clean, mcp-server rebuilt 10:30:50Z (tool count 160->161), raw-probe confirmed callable {released:false,lock_not_found}. (2) cowork-flow d88045c1 — leader-lock.md Step 0b now: claimed=false -> heartbeat probe ok=false -> task_force_release_orphan; released=true -> re-claim & proceed (restart-orphan); released=false -> live peer, silent exit. 80L<120L cap. Recurring-bug escalation honored (4th touch -> architect root-cause before any blind fix per feedback_recurring_bug_escalation). Operator Cowork-refresh paste required to propagate to running cowork agents.

done_verified.desc:
RECURRING ROOT-CAUSE (PLAN-ONLY — do NOT implement; route design to agents-architect). Surfaced across 3 consecutive maintenance passes 2026-06-13: agents commit to local main but rarely push, so origin/main perpetually lags — observed 27, then 30+ unpushed commits in ~2h windows (PO RAW-VERIFIED 2026-06-13T12:18Z: `git rev-list --count origin/main..main` = 30), forcing a rebase+push reconciliation every cycle. This is the symptom being cleared manually each pass; fix the cause.

ROOT-CAUSE DIRECTION (PO investigation): commit and push are SPLIT across skills. The generic `.claude/skills/commit/SKILL.md` HAS a push step (Step 3 `git push origin main`) but it is a BARE push with NO rebase-retry guard — under the known concurrent-commit-race it fails non-fast-forward and just errors, so it is unreliable. The HIGH-FREQUENCY commit paths — maintenance-lane `.claude/skills/commit-boundary/SKILL.md`, the mutex-guarded notebook-commit pattern (`.claude/skills/commit-mutex/SKILL.md`), and per-agent notebook commits embedded in flow docs (e.g. docs/agents/po/flow/main.md L134-140: `git add` + `git commit` only) — DO NOT PUSH AT ALL. So every notebook/orch-state commit (the bulk of commit volume) lands local-only and origin lags by construction.

CANDIDATE FIXES TO EVALUATE (architect picks/scopes; must NOT create push-storm races — respect lessons: concurrent commit race=serialize parallel workers share index, merge-gate cherry-pick serialize, commit-mutex):
(1) Add an explicit push step to the commit-boundary / commit-mutex SSOT so every committing agent pushes its OWN work, WRAPPED in a rebase-retry guard (`git push || (git pull --rebase origin main && git push)`, bounded retries) reusing the existing commit-mutex window so the push is serialized — no new race surface. PREFERRED on first read: push happens inside the already-serialized mutex window, attribution stays with the committing agent, no separate daemon.
(2) Periodic auto-push cron/hook that pushes accumulated local main on a short interval (decouples push from commit; single pusher = naturally race-free, but adds a cron + latency + a new always-on component; reconcile against existing cron inventory in docs/data/system-map.json).
(3) post-commit git hook that pushes — REJECT-LEANING: fires on EVERY commit under high concurrency = push-storm + non-fast-forward churn, directly violates concurrent-commit-race lesson unless gated behind the same mutex (then it is just option 1 relocated to a hook).

DEDUP: PO searched backlog/active_sprints/in_progress/review/done/done_verified — NO existing push/sync/origin-lag/unpushed/rebase task. This is genuinely new.

DELIVERABLE (architect): a design brief in docs/architecture-briefs/ choosing approach (1 vs 2, scoping the rebase-retry guard + mutex reuse + bounded-retry + race-safety proof), naming the single SSOT location for the push step, and listing every commit path that must adopt it. Then pm decomposes + agent-father implements the skill/flow edits. CONSTRAINT: do NOT touch docs/agents/*/init.md (agents confirmed active there). Acceptance: after fix, `git rev-list --count origin/main..main` stays bounded (target ≤ small N) across a full maintenance cycle with NO manual rebase+push reconciliation, and NO push-storm / non-fast-forward error spam in logs.
